result.title: Multi-Token Random-Walk Learning via Meeting-Triggered Information Exchange
result.summary: Random walk (RW)-based algorithms are widely used in decentralized learning due to their low communication overhead and scalability. While most existing methods rely on a single token, multiple tokens can explore the network in parallel and exchange information upon meeting. However, the fundamental benefits of such meeting-triggered interactions remain unclear. In this work, we investigate multi-token RW learning under two information exchange policies: \textsc{Average-Gradient} and \textsc{Average-Model}, which average stochastic gradients and updated models, respectively, when tokens meet. We establish iteration complexity lower bounds for non-convex, convex, and strongly convex objectives on complete graphs, which apply to both exchange policies. Compared with single-token RW learning, the scaling factor in these bounds is reduced by a factor of $m^2$ for non-convex and convex objectives, and by an exponentially in $m$ for strongly convex objectives, where $m$ denotes the number of tokens. Numerical experiments reveal distinct behaviors of the two policies under two performance criteria: mean-token loss (the average loss across all tokens) and best-token loss (the minimum loss across all tokens). \textsc{Average-Model} achieves lower mean-token loss and is relatively insensitive to the network-to-token ratio $N/m$, where $N$ is the number of nodes. In contrast, \textsc{Average-Gradient} achieves lower best-token loss but exhibits a trade-off between parallel exploration and gradient interference as $N/m$ decreases.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究去中心化学习中的多 token 随机游走，比较 token 相遇时「平均梯度」与「平均模型」两种信息交换策略，在完全图上给出非凸、凸与强凸目标的迭代复杂度下界，并实验对比两者在平均 token 损失与最优 token 损失上的差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 多 token 并行探索、相遇触发交换以及「并行探索 vs 梯度干扰」的权衡，可能为 LVR 中多个并行 latent 假设的信息交换、聚合与按均值/最优评价提供概念类比，具体对应关系可供核查。
